newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries open unch to lower before durables.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries open unch to lower before durables.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices opened unchanged to narrowly lower on Friday, awaiting economic data.
"The market is biding its time, waiting for durable goods," said James Blumenthal, economist at MCM Moneywatch.

The September durable goods orders report, due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT, should reflect a bounce after August's decline, economists believe. In Reuters' poll, the average forecast was for a two percent orders gain after a 3.2 percent August drop. Without defense-related items, orders are forecast at up 1.3 percent in September after a 3.6 percent fall in August.
"The durable goods series is very volatile and it can surprise the market, so there's the potential for that today and the market might react to a surprise," Blumenthal said.

How much of an orders rebound occurred in September "will help set the tone" for the market, said Kim Rupert, economist at MMS International "The two percent rise we expect should give the market a slight bullish bias."

At midmorning, the markets data on sales on September sales of existing homes. Those are expected to have occurred at a 4.11 million annualized rate, according to a Reuters poll of economists, tapering off from 4.13 million in August.
Two-year notes were down 1/32 to 99-27/32, yielding 5.96 percent. Five-year notes were unchanged at 99-25/32, yielding 6.30 percent.
The 6-1/2 percent ten-year note was down 2/32 to 99-13/32, yielding 6.58 percent.
The 6-3/4 percent 30-year bond was down 3/32 to 98-20/32, yielding 6.86 percent.
